editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.16, Definition 4.16.1. Connected indexing categories are nonempty, and their object sets are one equivalence class under zigzags of morphisms.

definitions.text: A category I is connected if it is nonempty and each pair of its objects can be joined by a finite sequence of morphisms whose directions may alternate.
A limit or colimit of a diagram is called connected when its indexing category is connected; this is a property of the index category rather than the limiting object.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: connected limit or colimit

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.5, Definition 10.5.1. Finitely generated and finitely presented modules have different finite generators-and-relations criteria.

definitions.text: An R-module M is finitely generated if a finite list m_1,…,m_n generates all of M by R-linear combinations; equivalently there is an R-linear surjection R^n→M.
An R-module M is finitely presented if it admits an exact sequence R^m→R^n→M→0 with m,n finite; finitely many generators and defining relations therefore suffice.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Fields 9.5, Definition 9.5.1, distinguishing a field's numerical characteristic from its smallest subfield.

definitions.text: The characteristic of a field F is the least positive integer n with n·1_F=0 when such an integer exists, and otherwise equals zero; a positive characteristic must be prime.
The prime subfield of F is its unique smallest subfield, isomorphic to Q in characteristic zero and to F_p in characteristic p>0.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Algebra 10.157, Definition 10.157.1 and Lemma 10.157.4. Serre's R_k and S_k conditions concern different invariants; their R_1/S_2 conjunction tests normality.

definitions.text: A Noetherian ring R satisfies (R_k) if the localization R_p is regular at each prime p of height at most k.
A Noetherian ring R satisfies (S_k) when depth(R_p) is at least min(k,dim R_p) for every prime ideal p.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Serre S_k for rings

definitions.text: A finite R-module M has property (S_k) if depth(M_p)≥min(k,dim Supp(M_p)) for all primes p of a Noetherian ring R.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Serre S_k for modules

definitions.text: A Noetherian ring R is normal if and only if it has (R_1) and (S_2), meaning regularity in codimension one and the corresponding lower bounds on local depths.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Topology 5.4, Definition 5.4.1 and Lemma 5.4.2, where separatedness is the relative closed-diagonal property.

definitions.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is separated when the image of its diagonal map X→X×_Y X is closed in that fibre-product topological space.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.28, Formal properties. The section discusses compatibility and composition of functors and natural transformations already introduced elsewhere, without independently defining a new object called 'formal properties'.
Checked Stacks Categories 4.17, Definitions 4.17.1 and 4.17.3. Cofinality corresponds to connected nonempty comma categories (j↓H), and initiality is the dual notion.

definitions.text: A functor H:I→J is cofinal if for every j in J the comma category (j↓H), whose objects are maps j→H(i), is nonempty and connected by finite zigzags.
A functor H:I→J is initial if for every object j of J the comma category (H↓j), consisting of maps H(i)→j, is nonempty and connected.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Fields 9.17, including its descriptions of roots of unity and primitive roots as elements of a specified multiplicative order.

definitions.text: An nth root of unity in a field F is an element ζ satisfying ζ^n=1; all such elements form a subgroup μ_n(F) of F×.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: nth root of unity

definitions.text: A primitive nth root of unity in a field F is an element ζ of multiplicative order exactly n.
